facts.fact: The Ministry of Communication Technologies' Mobile ID (E-Houwiya) FAQ describes a national digital identity in use for secure online login and electronic signature, free to Tunisian citizens aged 18 or over holding a national ID card.

The ministry's FAQ says Mobile ID login or e-signature is integrated in many government portals and platforms, listing 18 including e-cnam, the CNSS portal, the national business register, the tax administration's e-patente portal and the national administrative services portal.

The ministry's FAQ says citizens at home or abroad can bind Mobile ID to their phone through the E-Houwiya mobile app and use it to log in and sign documents electronically with the same legal value as a handwritten signature.

TUN.note: Birth extract named only as an online service reached through Mobile ID; no register link stated.

facts.fact: The ministry's FAQ lists Law No. 83 of 9 August 2000 on electronic exchanges and e-commerce as part of the legal framework for the digital identity, which gives its e-signature the legal value of a handwritten one.

The FAQ lists ministerial orders of 19 July 2001 on the technical data for electronic certification certificates and on the specifications of the electronic signature creation system, amended on 21 February 2018.

TUN.note: Lists platforms using Mobile ID login but does not say what services can be completed online or give a count of services or use.
ANCE and CNI support Mobile ID integration, but nothing is said of who operates or owns the national ID system.
Registers appear only as portals accepting Mobile ID login, not as keyed on the national ID number.
Describes Mobile ID, a credential obtained with the national ID card, not the national ID system itself.
Portals accept Mobile ID login; none is said to check people against the national ID.

facts.fact: The ministry's FAQ lists Government Order No. 777 of 5 October 2020 on the conditions and procedures for applying Decree-Law No. 31 of 2020 on electronic exchange of data between public bodies and their dealers and among bodies.

TUN.note: ANCE and CNI are named as giving integration support only; no statement of who runs or built a system.
